title: Iceberg Quantum Validates Pinnacle 1.2 Architecture with Crevasse QLDPC Decoder to Reduce RSA-2048 Factoring Resources - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Iceberg Quantum's Pinnacle 1.2 uses its new Crevasse QLDPC decoder (4 microseconds per round) to directly simulate trillions of error-correction cycles, validating logical error rates below 10^-12 needed for RSA-2048 factoring. Updated estimates put RSA-2048 at 72,000 physical qubits in 3.7 days at p = 10^-3 (48,000 qubits in 0.98 days at p = 10^-4) with a 1-microsecond cycle, and 99,000 qubits in 5.0 days on its Frozen Pinnacle superconducting variant.

insights.claim: Iceberg Quantum's Pinnacle 1.2 uses direct circuit-level simulations of QLDPC codes to validate logical error rates below 10^-12 per logical qubit-cycle, the threshold needed to run 2048-bit RSA factoring.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Moves RSA-breaking resource estimates from extrapolation to simulated validation, tightening the timeline debate for post-quantum migration.
insights.locator: Fault-tolerant quantum architecture startup Iceberg Quantum

insights.claim: Iceberg Quantum's Crevasse QLDPC decoder averages 4 microseconds of decoding latency per error-correction round, fast enough to execute trillions of simulated cycles directly instead of relying on statistical extrapolation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Fast QLDPC decoding is a key enabler for QLDPC architectures, a competitive alternative to surface codes.
insights.quote: Crevasse achieves an average decoding latency of 4 microseconds per error-correction round
insights.locator: The breakthrough is enabled by Crevasse

insights.claim: Across one trillion simulated samples, Iceberg Quantum observed only three logical errors on its d = 16 [[254,14,16]] code at p = 10^-3 (logical error rate 2 x 10^-13) and zero logical errors on its d = 10 [[126,12,10]] code at p = 10^-4 (<= 3 x 10^-13).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Concrete code parameters give a benchmark to compare against surface-code-based fault-tolerance roadmaps.
insights.locator: To establish these metrics, Iceberg Quantum

insights.claim: Pinnacle 1.2 estimates RSA-2048 can be broken with 72,000 physical qubits in 3.7 days at physical error rate p = 10^-3, or 48,000 physical qubits in 0.98 days at p = 10^-4, assuming a 1-microsecond code cycle time (atomic/photonic).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sub-100k-qubit estimates for RSA-2048 sharpen the urgency of post-quantum cryptography migration for banks, crypto and governments.
insights.quote: 72,000 physical qubits in 3.7 days at a physical error rate of p = 10-3
insights.locator: The breakthrough is enabled by Crevasse

insights.claim: For trapped-ion systems with a 1-millisecond code cycle, Pinnacle 1.2 estimates RSA-2048 needs 714,000 physical qubits for 29 days at p = 10^-4, or 2.1 million physical qubits for 32 days at p = 10^-3.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Slow cycle times impose a roughly 10x qubit penalty, a structural disadvantage for trapped-ion modalities in cryptanalysis-scale workloads.

insights.claim: Using smaller code distances in Pinnacle 1.2 cuts spatial overhead by about 40% and temporal overhead by about 30% versus Pinnacle 1.0 benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Resource estimates for cryptographically relevant quantum computers keep falling between releases, compressing Q-day timelines.

themes.theme: Magic states and Frozen Pinnacle for superconducting hardware

insights.claim: Iceberg Quantum verified complete modular exponentiation circuits against Pinnacle models using forced-gap post-selection for state injection, achieving injection error rates of (1.3 +/- 0.3) x 10^-6 at d = 10 and output magic-state failure rates near 3.5 x 10^-11.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: End-to-end verified circuits make the RSA estimate more credible than component-level extrapolations.
insights.locator: The team verified complete modular exponentiation

insights.claim: Applied to Frozen Pinnacle, a variant for superconducting systems with fixed degree-8 connectivity, the improved compilation reduces RSA-2048 requirements to 99,000 physical qubits and a 5.0-day runtime at p = 10^-3.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Puts superconducting vendors within roughly 100k qubits of RSA-2048 under QLDPC, relevant to Google and IBM roadmap comparisons.
insights.locator: The team verified complete modular exponentiation
